summary: Tested the admin-editable mode names feature end to end. Backend: 13/13 pytest pass. GET/POST /api/admin/mode_names admin-only (403 for players, 401 when logged out). POST merges new names with existing ones, collapses extra whitespace, rejects empty, whitespace-only, >20-char and unknown-key names with 400 and saves nothing when any field is invalid. /api/modes/status returns names. The names are saved in the db.meta mode_names doc. UI: the Moderation Mode Names panel works: 5 inputs, Save disabled at first, enabled after a change, disabled when any field is empty, 20-char maxLength, 'Mode names saved.' toast, values still there after reload. After renaming to Arcade/Competitive/Mega Brawl/Squad/Training: Lobby buttons show ARCADE, COMPETITIVE MATCH, MEGA BRAWL, TRAINING. Party panel shows SQUAD, ARCADE, COMPETITIVE @ BRONZE. Practice selector shows TRAINING RANGE. Casual match loading title shows ARCADE. HUD timer label shows ARCADE. Profile history badges show ARCADE. Names restored to defaults at the end.

action_items: Use mn('casual', true) for the 'CASUAL · FFA' chip in the Lobby quick-queue toast
Use the mode names in the FriendsModal queue status labels (bigffa/ranked/casual)

critical_code_review_comments: Backend implementation is clean: validation is done before saving, so a request with any invalid field changes nothing, and the 30s sync loop keeps pods in step.
Not tested in a live match: ranked HUD label (COMPETITIVE), MatchResultOverlay header and PublicProfileModal badges. They use the same modeName() getters as the screens that were checked.

success_rate.frontend: 100% of requested surfaces (2 minor missed spots found)

seed_data_creation: Temporarily formed party partyleader+partyfollower via API, then both left. Mode names restored to defaults.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Mode names live in db.meta _id=mode_names. Admin panel is on /admin/reports. Always restore the defaults after tests. Casual queue fills in about 6s, so a casual match starts quickly with player1.
